If you want to know what I did precisely on those days, I can tell you what I did, how I treated my tasks. From both areas of activity, I can tell you how I related to the subordinate units. Ask me specific questions and I'll give you specific answers where I was engaged on those particular days.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, I guess I'm having a hard time understanding how you could deal with your subordinate units if you, Momir Nikolic, didn't know what those units were tasked under the order that was drafted and approved by your own commander. And by your own admissions, you never communicated with the commander or with the chief of staff to know what was going on with respect to the battle on Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It's not a question. It's argumentative, and it's badgering the witness. I've tried not to object to these, but that must be about the 50th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, I think your question has a point. Just ask that question. We'll get your point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your testimony now is that even though you did not communicate with your commander, even though you did not know what plan he had put into action, you were nonetheless tasking your subordinates during those critical days on the attack of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One could put it that way, Mr. Karnavas. The intelligence part of the activities have a permanent character, an ongoing character. My subordinate officers in the professional sense, not in terms of the chain of command, are assistant commanders for intelligence and security in the battalions. The monitoring of the enemy, gathering intelligence on the enemy, the respective zones of intelligence responsibility, and all the other details, these are things that are set and fixed long ahead of time for all units. And it's not a question of any combat operations taking place or not. However, the grade of readiness is stepped up, in a manner of speaking, in such units as are gathering intelligence. For example, in the battalions, patrols, observers, and observation posts are assigned, and these are the bodies that work on gathering intelligence on a permanent basis. It doesn't matter whether there's an ongoing combat operation underway or not. They always do it, all the time. The assistant chief for security and intelligence had the task to sift the information received from those subordinate officers and check their authenticity, verify that intelligence, in order to be able to then report to the -- their superior command. And I would have been the person reported to at the superior command, at the brigade command.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Let me interrupt you here.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just briefly, Mr. Karnavas, please, if you allow me --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, the question is this: Do you have a superior command?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. He asked a very broad question with some reference -- negative references. I think the witness appears to be just trying to answer the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, allow the witness to finish his answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Go ahead. Then, if you could after you finish, tell me if you have a superior command, or had one during those days that you recognised.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'm going to object to the form of that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Karnavas, as I was saying, and I didn't finish my explanation in response to your question with respect to the continuity of the gathering of intelligence, I said that in the subordinate units there is an officer which professionally speaking is linked to me. And he has his own plan for the gathering of intelligence regardless of whether there is combat going on or not and that he also has reconnaissance organs, or rather organs in charge of gathering intelligence within the frameworks of his units, companies, platoons, whatever. And he also has his reconnaissance and reconnoitering points from which he is able to reconnoiter and monitor the enemy. And he does all that, Mr. Karnavas, in the area of responsibility of the battalion itself, and that area or zone, professionally speaking, is called the area of intelligence responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So once these organs have become involved, once this intelligence has been gathered, those organs send out their intelligence information to the office and the battalion, and he is called the assistant commander for of the commander for intelligence and security affairs. And he is in the command sense directly subordinate to the battalion commander. Professionally speaking, I am the officer who gives him instructions, who prepares him, instructs him, trains him, proposes him for further training and so on and so forth. So the information that comes to me from those professional organs, from the battalion command, I myself process, I systematise them, I classify them, I determine their authenticity, reject those which I consider to be incorrect or not authentic sources. And once I have done all that, I make my own evaluations. I write my evaluations down. I write down my notes and send out intelligence information which is reliable. And once it comes -- reaches the commander in the evening for a meeting he might convene, when my turn comes to report to him, I say "commander, sir, on the basis of the intelligence gathered from the 2nd infantry battalion, I have the following information: The distribution of enemy forces is such. They have launched operations on such and such an axis, troops deployed in such a place. We have undertaken the following steps. And I propose that the following be undertaken, that we intensify our reconnaissance work, our patrolling, sending out reconnaissance patrols," and so on and so forth. So that, Mr. Karnavas, is an entire process which is an ongoing one in the units, and it is the continuous task that has to be accomplished. And in view of this ongoing nature of this task, it is my prime task as assistant commander or head of the staff for intelligence and security, is to have a sufficient fund of intelligence at my beck and call to present to the commander on the basis of which he will be able to make the relevant decisions which means decisions which will then be based and founded on correct information, the right kind of intelligence. But of course, we can never say with absolute certainty that the intelligence gathered about the enemy are absolutely correct. So that would be my explanation to the series of questions you posed a moment ago. Thank you, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So there was nothing to report to the commander on the 6th because you didn't report to him, did you?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, I wish to say the following: Intelligence, vis-a-vis the commander and the superior command follow two lines. Intelligence is sent up in two ways. One is the intelligence line, and the second one is the chain of command line. So the professional body, the assistant commander for intelligence and is security affairs from the 2nd Battalion would inform me. However, the commander of the unit, the battalion commander, reports to the commander directly or through his duty officer if he is unable to establish contact with the commander. Therefore, everything that I had at my disposal, all the intelligence at my disposal at that point in time went both to me and to the commander. There was no request made to me for me to have to report on a special -- in a special way when there is no separate request. So in cases of that kind, it is up to me to assume that this is automatic through the chain of command and that there's no need for me to report up to him. Had I been given special instructions to do so or had special intelligence been required, then I would have found a way to send it up to the forward command post either by the officer on duty or in some other way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So as far as you are concerned you, Momir Nikolic, chief of security and intelligence, on the 6th, you did not have anything to report to your commander based on your assessment?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of my assessments and evaluations for that period of time, for that particular day, I did not have any new information to provide, any new information coming to me that I should have informed the commander about. At least in the initial stage of the operations, if we're talking about the 6th because the attack in fact began on the 6th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Then of course, because you didn't report to him on the 7th, based on your intelligence, there was nothing to communicate to your commander with respect to intelligence that you had gathered from your sources in the field and from your subordinates?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say now for sure that there was nothing on the 7th, 8th, 9th, or 10th. But during that period of time, all I can say is - I'm not certain about Commander Blagojevic, but people would come to the brigade command, the officers at the forward command post at Pribicevac. And I can't say with certainty whether I told him something at that time during that period or not. But what I do know is that there were no requests made of me. I was not asked to supply any additional intelligence or information or data.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I didn't ask you whether you were requested from your commander. Is it not a fact based on your earlier statement where you said you had no, absolutely no contact physical or by other means of communication with your commander on the 6th, 7th, 8th, 9th, 10th, and the 11th, that you did not report anything to him with respect to intelligence based on the assessments that you were making?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, I think I've already explained that once. Everything that was of interest with respect to intelligence went to the duty officer directly from the commander to the subordinate units or to me in the brigade command and intelligence. And I think that I've already spoken about this and said that that was not the only way -- it's not the only way of informing the commander directly. Because there are situations when you cannot do this, you can't see the commander directly to inform him. And that this kind of reporting goes through the duty officer because, among other things, that is one of the tasks that he has to do. He conveys to the commander information of this kind. So it is the duty officer that is in communication with the commander all the time and knows where the commander is to be found at all times.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What impediments, if any, prevented you - the 6th, the 7th, the 8th, the 9th, the 10th, the 11th - prevented you directly, the chief of intelligence and security, your commander about the intelligence situation on the ground as the information was coming to you from your sources and subordinates?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, first of all, those were not my sources. So the gathering of intelligence and sending out intelligence from the unit, because it's a brigade -- a unit of the brigade, if you want the real truth, why should the 1st infantry battalion be more my source than the commander's source? It is our source.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. But my question is you say today as you sit here that your subordinates would send the information up to you. Right? That was part of your answer.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Assistant commanders for intelligence and security affairs from the battalion, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Are they your subordinates?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the professional sense, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, what other sense are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Subordination can also be in the command realm, so I am not their commander. I am not in command of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We are talking about the information that these folks have in relation to intelligence. Okay? Are you with me on this point? This is all I'm talking about. Are they not or do you not see them as subordinates to you where they send information from down, up to Momir Nikolic, chief of security and intelligence?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas. The rules of service stipulate it in that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And that's how you understand them?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How, in what way?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The way you described it. I'll move on. Too complicated. Now, once that information comes to you, Momir Nikolic, chief of security and intelligence, or intelligence and security, you decide -- you filter that information. And you decide what's solid information what's iffy information, maybe not so good, or potentially good, but not quite sure, and what's very important, that you might need to send up the chain of command? Did I hear you correctly that you do some sort of analysis of your own?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you didn't understand me at all, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Let me understand you. All of the information that comes to you - all of it - you send up to your higher command?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. You decide what information, if any, if any, you're going to send up to your command -- superior command?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Perhaps counsel doesn't realise it, but he is now shouting at the witness which I don't think is necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I agree with you. Mr. Karnavas, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I will --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Let me say a few words.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I believe that the witness has answered your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Maybe you did not grasp that. Because he told us there are two channels. Maybe the intelligence officer in the battalion directly contact the commander, at the same time informed him. If there is nothing new, he will not send a separate report to his commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And the fact is established that the witness said that there was nothing new, so he does not do anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: It's very clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Let's look at the rules.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which rules, Mr. Karnavas?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... Rules. Please look at Rule 118. We looked at it yesterday, if you could look at it very briefly. Now Rule 118, it says here: "The intelligence organ is responsible for and organises intelligence support for combat action." This was a combat action, was it not, in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, did you organise for this particular combat mission the intelligence support? Yes or no? And I don't want to hear about the existing process that existed. I'm familiar with that. For this particular order, did you organise intelligence support?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean security for combat operations?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go back. The first line, 118. We'll go from --

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It says here: "Intelligence organise - that would be you - is responsible for and organises intelligence support for combat actions." That's what it says, does it not?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Srebrenica, the attack on Srebrenica, was a combat action, was it not?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: There was, based -- on July 5th, 1995, an order which spelled out the participation of the Bratunac Brigade in this combat action. Is that not a fact?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The order that I saw, is that the order to the Bratunac Brigade? Is that what you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The one we have been speaking about all morning, yes.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, based on that order which involves a combat action, did you as the head of the intelligence organ of the Bratunac Brigade, the chief of intelligence and security, did you organise intelligence support for this particular combat action? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of that order, the one you're talking about, I did not because I did not have it. However, I took all steps required by me so that -- as to provide intelligence security, to have it function as it had been doing in the previous period.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. You didn't have the order. Might I ask why did you not get the order, look for the order, ask for the order?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Sounds very familiar, Your Honour. I don't think the second time around the debate, anything's going to change. It's all been discussed before.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I don't believe I asked why.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll move on, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: -- I don't think this witness could answer your question because at least there's not his name on it. There's a distribution list. There's not his name on it. It's not his problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. May I ask him if he wanted to look for the order, would he know where to look for it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, if he does not know there's an order, how could he ask for that order?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay, okay, Your Honour. Maybe I'll lay a foundation on that one. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It says here, the next sentence: "It continuously monitors and assesses the enemy and reports the enemy conditions to everyone concerned in the command." That's the second sentence.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas. And that is precisely what I was saying a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I just be allowed to continue, that is precisely the explanation I gave a moment ago, that it was a continuous process and not a job done over one, two, or three days prior to the operation. It is a process, a continuous one which is an ongoing one, put into practice constantly and engaging organs responsible for doing that kind of work.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I could not agree with you more. But it says here that you are "monitoring and assessing the enemy" - that's one part - "and reports," and reports the enemy's conditions to everybody concerned in the command." "To everybody." Question: Would the commander be someone included in that "everybody" that's in here?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, of course he would.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, it suggests to the commander or chief of staff the procedures and resources for intelligence support for the brigade." I take it since you had no communications with your commanding officer, your commander, during that period, 6th, 7th, 8th, 9th, 10th, 11th, there are no suggestions that you needed to make with respect to procedures and resources for intelligence support for the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, with your permission, might I be allowed to say the following, because Mr. Karnavas has given quite the erroneous interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may interrupt here for a second. The question was very clear. I pointed a section in the third sentence which talks about suggesting. "It suggests, commands" and I put it into the context, during that five- or six-day period. Since he had no contact with his commander, might we conclude that he had nothing to suggest to the commander with respect to procedure and resources for intelligence support during the campaign on Srebrenica? I don't see how that -- what's so complex about this.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Karnavas, you read out "the commander or chief of staff the procedure and resources for intelligence support for the brigade. It suggests to the commander or chief of staff, et cetera."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas. However, what you and I are reading now relates to the process taking part before the order is written. It is then that I propose to the commander or the chief of staff the way in which and resources and intelligence support for the brigade. It's a process which I propose before the order is actually given.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, could you please look at 359. 359 in the brigade rules.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: For the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I apologise. For the record, we're still dealing with the same document which has been marked for identification purposes as P83. And I'm referring to Article 359, which is on page 97. And let me read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It says: "The brigade commander constantly monitors the situation and influences the course of the battle by issuing new or additional tasks. He makes his decision on the basis of reports submitted by subordinate officers and his personal observations." Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. You said point 359, did you?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a few moments to let me look at that. Yes, I've found it. 359. There are two sentences.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, a combat situation is a fluid situation, is it not?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know precisely what you mean by "a fluid situation" as referring to a combat situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, you have a plan, but nothing ever really goes or rarely does it ever go exactly to plan. Things change as the battle is fought.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can only assume that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let's assume that that's the situation with battles, that even though you might have the perfect plan, something might go wrong. Okay? Now, it seems to me --

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's always possible, isn't it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay, all right.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not necessarily, not necessarily.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Sometimes it's better, sometimes it's worse.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right, if you say so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In any event, the commander needs to be aware of the information that's coming in because he needs to adjust his tactics and his plan according to the situation.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And so, that may require even after you have made suggestions to the commander based on the continuation of the situation and based on information that you gather to make further suggestions to the commander as the chief of intelligence of security. No?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not what it means, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Well, then we'll move on. Further down in the same paragraph, I'm just going to skip down to the last sentence, it says: "It controls the reconnaissance unit" -- I'm referring to 118 now, I'm back to 118 now. I'm referring to 118. "It controls the reconnaissance unit, it monitors the ability, training..." And it goes on so on and so forth. Now, in this particular order, and I'm referring to the order of 5 July 1995 which, for identification purposes, is D17/1, I believe, if I'm not mistaken, in 5.5 of the order makes reference to a reconnaissance platoon. Now, I don't know whether you have any engagement or any contact or any responsibilities with respect to this platoon. But in reading 118, it might give someone that suggestion. Or would I be wrong, that you control the reconnaissance unit?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think I still owe Mr. Karnavas one answer in relation to gathering intelligence. Mr. Karnavas, the commander by his order defines the method and the forces gathering intelligence before combat operations commence. He also defines the method and the strength of the forces gathering intelligence during combat, which means that the commander makes sure that he has both the resources and the forces and he defines the methods in which intelligence is gathered. I hope -- I have not gone through this order very carefully, but I certainly hope that in this order, too, the commander defined the way things should evolve before combat operations and during combat operations, who and which units should be gathering intelligence. I hope it is clearly defined. So for the sake of clarification, you insisted on having a clarification -- can you please ask me a specific question related to this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, I think Mr. Karnavas asked you a specific question. He asked: "Did you control the reconnaissance unit?" It's simple.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am not sure that there was a reconnaissance platoon or a reconnaissance unit at that time at all. I am really not sure because throughout that period, and earlier, there were problems with the unit that we used as the reconnaissance platoon. And I'm really not sure. I'm not sure. I'm not sure that there was a reconnaissance platoon in the brigade at all or whether it was established during that period. But I can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you have another question, Your Honour? Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But getting back to the question that I asked and His Honour asked you, were you in charge of the reconnaissance unit, whether -- in general? I mean, if one had existed, would you be the person, as the chief of the intelligence organ, to be in charge of that unit as it's designated in 118 of the rules?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whenever there is a reconnaissance platoon of the brigade, professionally speaking, I would be in charge of its work.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if we look at the order, and I'm going back to what has been previously marked as 17/1 for identification purposes - it's D17 - in paragraph 5.5, it makes reference to a reconnaissance platoon of the brigade. Can we assume, maybe even conclude, that since you have this in the order placed there by the commander himself, that a reconnaissance platoon existed at that time in the Bratunac Brigade of which you would have been in charge of or they would have been under your control?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that in the military and professional sense, I would have been in charge of it. But this does not mean that it was my task to run the platoon or to command the platoon. This would have been the case if it was part of the brigade. I would have had a responsibility towards that platoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. But from this order, does not the order itself reflect that there is indeed a reconnaissance platoon?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I see here, what it says is: "Reconnaissance platoon is to be held ready to repel the enemy's counterattack." If you can see that it actually says "the brigade's reconnaissance platoon" I don't know because within the composition of the 1st Battalion, and I think the 3rd Battalion, we had platoons that we referred to "reconnaissance platoons," but they were not linked to me professionally. Therefore, I can't use this to conclude that this was about the reconnaissance platoon of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So this is just about a reconnaissance platoon that may exist outside the Bratunac Brigade. That's your understanding?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not my understanding. According to the establishment, there were squads within a battalion. But the practical situation on the ground was different. For example, in the 3rd infantry battalion, there was a platoon referred to as a reconnaissance platoon or intervention platoon. In the 1st infantry battalion, you had the same unit but was not officially part of the establishment, because according to the establishment there should have been a squad and instead there was an intervention platoon or a reconnaissance platoon, or at least that's how they referred to themselves. I can't say with certainty. Therefore, at brigade level, as a unit attached to the staff, according to the establishment, yes, there was a reconnaissance platoon of the brigade. So that's what I had in mind. Of course, I didn't say that this was not from the composition of the brigade. This may as well have been one of the platoons from the subordinated battalions to the brigade, the 1st or the 2nd -- the 3rd. Even the 2nd Battalion had one such unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And would you have been responsible for any of those units in a situation such as the one envisaged in your commander's order?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I must say I can't really say for sure which unit this is. All I can see is that it says "reconnaissance platoon." If it said, for example, the reconnaissance platoon of the Bratunac Brigade, then I'd know for sure. If it said the reconnaissance squad of the 1st infantry battalion, I could know for sure. If it said the intervention or reconnaissance platoon of the 3rd infantry battalion, I would know for sure and then I could answer your question. This way, I cannot answer your question. I cannot possibly tell you whether I was in charge of a reconnaissance platoon which is not even specified. And I've never seen this order before, on top of that. Therefore I can't answer your question. I neither confirm nor deny anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. But the bottom line is there were units in the Bratunac Brigade which were reconnaissance units. Right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, I think that will lead us to nowhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You're probably right, Your Honour. You're probably right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: It's time for a break if you think it's the right time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: This would be a great time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, now we are in the period of July 6 to 11th. But that is the most crucial time period.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I hope we could come to July 11th and afterwards as soon as possible because those periods are the most relevant periods.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll resume at quarter to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Before we move on to the next topic, Mr. Nikolic, I just want to clarify a couple of points. Let's go back to the order of July 5. Please look at paragraph 5.1. This paragraph, does it not refer to the 1st infantry battalion of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well. Now, on the third paragraph, it says: "Reconnaissance platoon to be prepared to fend off enemy counterattack." That reference to the -- first of all, does it say that in your -- in Srpski? Can you see it?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. "Reconnaissance platoon to be prepared to fend off enemy counterattack."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And since that is in the section dealing with the 1st infantry battalion, one might assume that it's referring to a reconnaissance platoon of the 1st infantry battalion, would it not?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, the way this reads and within the framework of this text, this order, yes, you could say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if you could look at 5.2. This section refers to the 2nd infantry battalion of the Bratunac Brigade, does it not?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does. That's how it reads.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Again, in the third paragraph, if you will, does it not say: "Reconnaissance platoon to be in the area of the geographical area of..." And I guess it gives the coordinates. Does it not say that?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: From reading this paragraph, might we assume or conclude that it is making reference to a reconnaissance platoon within or of the 2nd infantry battalion of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course we might, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And finally, if we could look at 5.5, the one that we discussed previously at some length, does it not read: "Reconnaissance platoon of the brigade..." And then it continues on. Does it not say that?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas. This says "reconnaissance platoon of the brigade." Again, I wish to tell you that this is no sufficient indication for me, especially since it says "reconnaissance platoon of the brigade with L/r." I really have no idea what the abbreviation stands for, if you can please enlighten me on that, "L/r."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. I just wanted to confirm that what I have in English is what you see in Srpski or B/C/S as it's called here, that it says "reconnaissance platoon of the brigade."

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, "reconnaissance platoon of the brigade." That's what it says, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Might we assume or conclude that it's referring -- when it says "brigade" that it's referring to the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be a random conclusion for me to make. I could easily conclude that, that it's the Bratunac Brigade, or it's not. I could also conclude that I have no idea what the abbreviation stands for, L/r. What is it? I could make a number of conclusions. But I would not be certain of any of those conclusions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's move on. I could liked briefly - I underscore briefly - discuss the rules regarding your functions as the security organ, and then we'll go to the military police. So if you could look at, if you could have handy the "Rules of Services of Security Organs in the Armed Forces of the Socialist Federative Republic of Yugoslavia, 1984." And I'm referring to P84. I just want to go over some very -- a few articles. If you could look at, please -- first, are you familiar with this particular document?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say that this is the document that you had in your possession or available to you while you were serving as the head of intelligence and security of the Bratunac Brigade back in 1995?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. If we could look at -- I'm just going to go through some of these very quickly. Look at number 8. I just want to focus on the first couple lines. Tell me if your version in Srpski has what I see here in English. It says: "Security organs perform duties and tasks within the competence in accordance with their rights and duties as established by the law and the provisions of these rules and other regulations issued pursuant to the law..." And so on and so forth. Do you see that in number 8? I just read part of the -- it's one paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Might we assume that what this says is that your duties, that you must carry out your duties, perform your duties, in accordance with the law and the regulations?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And these would be one of those regulations, would they not?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm not a lawyer myself. I can't see a rule defined here. What I see defined is the standards according to which I must act and work, not being a lawyer myself, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, just for the sake of it, why don't you flip to the first page and read me the title of this document. It says: "Rules of Service." Right?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The front page reads: "Rules of Service of security organs in the armed forces of the Socialist Federative Republic of Yugoslavia," dated 1984. And then the front page also states: "Federal Secretariat for National Defence Military Secret Strictly Confidential File Number 2046UB1/3." That's what I can see on the front page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. Might we assume that these may be part of the rules that they're referring to, and this particular article that we're just discussing?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I understand your question, I'm afraid, Mr. Karnavas. Could you please repeat this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Why don't we go on to the next one. Article 9. It says here, I'll read the pertinent part: "In carrying out the duties and tasks under items 6 and 7 of these rules" - the ones that we're holding - "security organs may make contact directly with members of the armed forces and other citizens, military organs, and organs of sociopolitical communities, sociopolitical and other social organisations and organisations of associated labour..." And so on and so forth. Do you see Article 9?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: From reading that, might we conclude that you, as the head of security, had the right to have direct contact with, say, members of the Bratunac municipal government under this article?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, I would first take -- have to take a look at what paragraph 6 and 7 define in order to be able to answer your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. But with respect to 6 and 7, 6 speaks about your responsibilities, and 7 speaks about with whom you may participate.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, would you allow me to read all of paragraph 6 and 7, and then we can proceed. I partially read it, Mr. Karnavas. Not all of it, and in detail. But I get a general impression what of what points 6 and 7 contain. So if you could now repeat your question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: My question was if you, for instance, wanted to have contact with Mr. Deronjic in your official capacity as chief of security - I'm putting it in a concrete fashion although I'm using a hypothetical here - if you wanted to have direct contact with him, could you do so as it seems you might be able to under this article, article 9 of the rules of services of security organs?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the first part of your question. When it comes to the official connection between me and Deronjic. In what official capacity do you mean between me and Miroslav Deronjic? And then I'll be able to answer your question. What do you mean "contact in an official capacity"?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. The night of the 13th, the night of the 13th of July 1995, you've indicated that you had an opportunity to participate in a meeting with Mr. Deronjic in which -- where Colonel Beara was there, and I believe it was also Mr. Vasic or Colonel Vasic. It's late in the day, I'm getting a bit tired. Do you recall that? Do you recall stating --

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, obviously Colonel Beara is a superior officer from the main staff. So obviously, you could have direct contact with him or he contact with you. But there you were as head or the chief of the security sector of the Bratunac Brigade on that particular night having a direct contact with Mr. Deronjic who at the time was not in the military, but was there in a civilian capacity.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I can tell you is this: That I was able freely to communicate and come into contact with anybody in Bratunac, so I really don't see -- I could contact anybody including Deronjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay, but I'm talking professionally now. I know socially because a small town. Obviously you're going to have coffee or rakija or whatever. When you run into people, you can have contact. But professionally speaking in your official capacity, because after all, you were the chief of intelligence and security of the Bratunac Brigade, and formally you were, as we know, the acting commander of the Territorial Defence, member of the War Presidency in Bratunac, as was Mr. Deronjic. So my question is, in reading this article, Article 9, it would appear that in your official capacity you had every right under the law to meet with individuals such as Mr. Deronjic in his official capacity?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, I must say that I, in my official capacity, did not have any reason or need to meet with Deronjic because Deronjic -- I know the post he occupied during that period of time. I know what his position was. However, he, in my opinion, didn't mean anything in the military hierarchy. And so I didn't have any meetings with him, nor did I discuss anything of any importance with him. Of course, I'm not claiming that I don't know Miroslav Deronjic, and I'm not saying that Miroslav Deronjic is somebody whom I don't know. Miroslav Deronjic is my brother-in-law. I do know the man. But except for that night, that is to say, the 13th when Colonel Beara said he had a meeting with Miroslav Deronjic and that I should accompany him, at that period of time I had no need to consult Miroslav Deronjic, to have a meeting with him or anything of that nature at all. Had I had any need of doing so, if the situation was such that somebody had ordered me or suggested that I meet with him, had there been a need to do so, I would have probably met him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. The night of the 13th, you were summoned, if I could use that word, or requested to meet with Colonel Beara. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Upon meeting him, you learned that you would be meeting along with him, Colonel Beara, Mr. Deronjic on that particular night. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Karnavas. When I received information to report to Colonel Beara, there was no mention of, nor did I know that I would be meeting Mr. Deronjic at all. I was given a concrete assignment as to what I was to do then.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you meet with Deronjic that night? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That night, I was in the office, which is where Mr. Deronjic has his headquarters. That night, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Those were the headquarters of the SDS. Is that it?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: He held an official capacity at that time in that community?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the municipality, no, he didn't have any official post. I mean, in the administration, the organs of administration. Now, if you think he was president of the SDS or the main board, yes, he was that too, if that's what you have in mind. But he didn't have any official capacity in the organs of administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So -- now at some point he became the commissioner or the komesar, however you call it, of Srebrenica. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: On the night of the 13th, do you know whether Mr. Deronjic had any contact with or from President Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I can tell you is that that evening, he did refer to Mr. Karadzic. That is what I knew then. And having looked through the documents and the intercepts, I know that he had a conversation with Mr. Karadzic because I read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. Now, when you met with Mr. Deronjic, who requested that meeting? Who set it up?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know who set it up, who organised the meeting, at whose initiative it was. I didn't even know before the meeting who was invited to attend the meeting before I arrived. All I can say is that I can confirm that I was taken to the meeting by Colonel Beara. I went at his request. Now, who actually organised the meeting and scheduled it, set it up, I really can't say because I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. When you were asked to go to the meeting with Colonel Beara, were you there in your official capacity as the chief of intelligence and security of the Bratunac Brigade, or were you there as Momir Nikolic, resident of Bratunac, or were you there as a subordinate to Colonel Beara?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, I was there -- I went to see Colonel Beara, in fact, at his request, at his invitation. So that then was a military act, the act of a soldier. He called up the communications centre and conveyed the message that I should report to him at the Bratunac centre. So I went there as a soldier because Colonel Beara was the chief of the main staff administration, and it was quite normal for me to respond to the invitation on the part of a superior officer from the security department of the main staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Might we conclude that Colonel Beara was back then in 1995 your superior officer, superior commander, when it came to issues of security?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection on the form of that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Officer, commander, these are very different things.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll break it down. I'll break it down, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Colonel Beara was with the main staff, was he not?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In the security sector, right?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Head of the security sector of the main staff?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: He had somebody above him?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Above him was the assistant commander of the main staff for information and intelligence and security, General Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The gentleman that I made reference to yesterday as the one that might have okayed your position when you became the -- when you joined the intelligence sector, when you were with the Territorial Defence, if you recall that? In any event, okay. Now, was Colonel Beara above or below you?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Colonel Beara, on the basis of the hierarchy and his position, was an officer of the superior command.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Below him, or below the superior command would be the Drina Corps. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, if you mean formation-wise, establishment-wise. The main staff is the top level, the level before is the Drina Corps command or the Drina Corps, or one of the corps. It doesn't matter which.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And then within the corps, you have the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the Bratunac Brigade is a unit within the composition of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, you as head of intelligence and security -- but let's focus on security. You as head of security, chief of security for the Bratunac Brigade, you were in essence part of the same organ which Beara belonged to, that is, the security organ. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was, sir, part of the intelligence security organ.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And so was --

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the level of brigade. So part of that organ at the level of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Did you look to Colonel Beara or did you see him, did you view him as a superior commander to you when it came to matters of security or to functions within the security organ?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Colonel Beara and no commanding officer did I see as being my superior commander. I felt that Colonel Beara and the officers superior to me from the Drina Corps command, that they were officers which indirectly or directly were responsible for the professional work and guidance of my own activities within the frameworks of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So did you feel free that night to decline Colonel Beara's invitation? Or did you think you had to go ahead and meet with him?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In principle, never, not in any situation did I refuse or decline an invitation from an officer in the superior command, whether direct or indirect, to go to a meeting if I was asked to do so. And so it was the same on this occasion. I didn't consider that I should decline.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Did you think that you had to inform your own commander that you had this invitation by Colonel Beara on night of the 13th to meet him in the middle of the town?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not at that point in time, I didn't consider that to be necessary, to report to the brigade commander. Because quite simply, I didn't know why Colonel Beara was asking me to come. I knew nothing specific. And I only want to say that if that were the case after every assignment I was given, that I ran to the commander, well, we would never get the job done. I'd go mad if I had to go and report back every half hour, every time I received a task or assignment or when a newly arisen situation arose, that I would run to the commander. That was not standard practice, Mr. Karnavas, and I considered that this invitation was quite legitimate and I should report to that commander officer. And that's what I did. I went there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And as you stated, you didn't know why he called you. He could have called you for rakija, pivo, beer, or maybe have an official meeting. Right? You didn't know at the time.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I didn't know the reason I had been asked to come. He could have invited me to partake of any of those things that you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. And then at some point after the meeting, after you met and spoke with him, with Beara, after you met with him, spoke with him, at some point, the two of you went to see Deronjic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment, Mr. Karnavas. I was very precise when I said when I went to the meeting, the office of Miroslav Deronjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That was before or after Zvornik, after your trip to Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The meeting with Mr. Beara, I went there after I had reported to him that I had executed his order having returned from Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So after Zvornik is when you went to -- you had this meeting with Beara and Deronjic.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And at that point, you were meeting with Beara and Deronjic based on the invitation that you had received earlier from Colonel Beara to meet him, and after having completed the tasks that he had issued you?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't really understand what you're question is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right, okay. When you were with Mr. Deronjic, did you feel compelled at that point, since you were meeting someone in the community who obviously was fairly important with respect to some pretty important matters, did you feel that you needed to contact your commander prior to having that meeting with Mr. Deronjic, Colonel Beara, and others?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I did not feel that I had to go to the command and report to the commander, and then to go back to attend the meeting in the presence of the commanding officer from the main staff who was part of the team of the main staff and who was present in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Were you there as Colonel Beara's subordinate at that particular time? Is that how you saw your role?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw my role as being the assistant commander for these affairs in the brigade who finds himself in the presence of a senior officer from the main staff attending a meeting. Of course, I can also say that somebody from the unit in the presence of these top-ranking officers always feels as if he was -- he were subordinate to these commanding officers. How else would one feel?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well. Now, if you could look at number 12. And I'm still referring to the Rules of Service. And it's P84 for identification. Rule number 12. Why don't you look if you locate it, and I'll read it, and tell me if I'm reading it correctly. "Security organs report on their work to their immediate superior and the security organs of the superior command units, institutions or staff, in accordance with the provisions of these rules." Is that what Article 12 has in the Srpski?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If we could focus on this a little bit, and I want to focus on the word "report." It says: "Report on their work to their immediate superior." Now, who is your immediate superior?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My immediate superior was the brigade commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And then it says: "And security organs of the superior commands..." Who might they be?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first superior command was the command of the Drina Corps which means that it was security department of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And who might that be? Who would head that department?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The head of security was Mr. Vujadin Popovic, a lieutenant-colonel. And in the intelligence department, there was Mr. Kosoric.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So -- now is there a particular order in which you need to report, to your understanding?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there is a particular order, Mr. Karnavas. On the accomplished assignments, you report to the commander of the unit from which the security organ is a part. And after that, you report to the -- inform the intelligence department or security department of the superior command.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So if I understand your answer, first you report to commander, your immediate commander, which is Colonel Blagojevic. And then, and only after then, do you report to the Drina Corps. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, 14. It says here: "When called up for exercises, members of security organs from the reserve strength of the armed forces verify combat readiness and other activity in combat units of the armed forces and perform tasks within the competence of the security organs in accordance with the regulations on the work of security organs." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I want to focus --

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read through it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I want to focus on the word or the term "reserve." You were a -- you were a reserve officer at the time, were you not?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: May we assume or conclude from reading Article 14 that as a reserve officer, having been called, mobilised, however you wish to use the term, whatever, you, too, were under the obligation to perform your tasks in accordance with the rules as everyone else?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not entirely sure that I have understood you correctly. However, the way I read this article, it doesn't apply to the state of war. What it says is "members of security organs from the reserve strength when called up for exercises, verify combat readiness and other activity in combat units," those are forms of exercise. It says "when called up for exercises, verifying combat readiness and other activity in combat units," or rather war units. This doesn't necessarily entail a state of war because you have combat units even in peacetime. And they are composed of officers. They have their own equipment. In combat units of the armed forces, again, called up for exercises, to verify combat readiness and perform tasks within the pretense of the security organs in accordance with the regulations, well, of course, when carrying out their tasks during these exercises, security organs implement tasks pursuant to regulations governing the work of security organs. That's perfectly normal. However, Mr. Karnavas, this does not apply to a state of war or a state of emergency. This merely explains what an officer who has been called up for a military exercise as part of his unit must abide by.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, as a reserve officer, a captain, is it not a fact that these rules apply to you while you were performing your duties as a chief of intelligence and security? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I've understood you fully. Can you please just repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, I will.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My apology.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Were there separate rules for reserve officers and, say, professional, active-duty officers, or do these rules, the ones that we're going through right now, apply to both?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, of course all officers called up to join units have certain tasks and duties. The regulations apply to all officers for any area of activity, and the same applies to security.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you. If you could look at now Article 16, it says here: "The security organ is directly subordinate to the commander officer of the command, unit, institution..." And so on and so forth. And it goes on: "And it is responsible to that officer for its work..." And so on and so forth. Might we assume or conclude from reading Article 16 that you were directly subordinate to Colonel Blagojevic when he was your commander of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay, so -- okay. We'll move on. We'll go to 18. And I'll --

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. "Security organ of the superior command, unit, institution, or staff of the armed forces provide specialist administrative services for security organs in subordinate commands, units, institutions, and staffs of the armed forces, provide assistance to these organs, and organise, direct, coordinate, and supervise their work." Might we conclude or assume, or assume and conclude, that these were, in fact, part of your responsibilities during the 6th, 7th, 8th, 9th, 10th, and 11th of July 1995?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we can't, Mr. Karnavas. We can't make that conclusion. Based on what it says here, I can -- I can only conclude between the relationship of the organ of the superior command, the unit of the institution or staff, and the subordinate officers in subordinate units or staffs. I can make conclusions about that relationship, and I can make conclusions regarding the duties between the superior officers from these organs and those from the subordinate units. But again, within the framework of these same bodies. These are the conclusions that I can make pursuant to Article 18. But none of these indicate any specific tasks. Only the relationship itself it defined here as far as I can see.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And did that relationship exist between the 6th, 7th, 8th, 9th, 10th, and 11th?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Article 22, please. The first paragraph says: "The senior officer of a command, unit, institution, or staff of the armed forces supervises the work of subordinate security organs according to the general regulations unless otherwise determined by these rules for the supervision of certain work by the security organ." What is your understanding of this particular article?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, my understanding is exactly how it reads. No different from that, exactly what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. Well, what exactly does it say?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you want me to read this back to you, the whole article?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, I don't think I need that. I'll go on to -- we'll get back to that. But first I want to cover 23. Take a look at 23, and I believe this refers to military police. And it says: "An officer of the security organ of a command, unit, institution provides specialist management for a military police unit." So I believe that's what you were referring to yesterday -- sometime yesterday. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It would be good for us to also read the second part, because that's a follow up to what I was talking about. It says that the officers of the staff or unit can use military police units and are responsible for the situation in that unit. I think that's the only right way to go about that because these form a whole. So I've explained that. I've explained my role in terms of providing guidance, professional guidance, regarding the military police unit as well as my powers, my authority in the same context. It all follows from this text.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if we could now turn to the -- since we're on the military police, if we could look at the regulations on the military police, and that has been marked previously for identification purposes D15/1. Just very briefly, if you could --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Are we about to break? 1.45? Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I have it in front of me, Mr. Karnavas, the rules.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If you could look at number 12, please. It says, and let me read it: "The officer in charge of the military unit and institution within whose establishment the military police unit is placed or to which it is attached commands and controls the military police." Can we assume or conclude that it is the brigade commander that's in charge of the military police?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's what the article says.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So if, say, the chief of security or chief of intelligence and security wanted to task military police of the brigade, he could not, or at least he should not do it without getting the authorisation from the commander. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The interpretation I'm getting is that you said if the chief of security wanted to task a military police unit, that's the interpretation I'm getting, that you actually said if the chief of security wishes to task the police to do something. I'm not really sure about the definition, what you meant, "task" them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Let's say Momir Nikolic, pick an example, as the chief of security wanted to use certain military police to perform a particular task that Momir Nikolic, chief of security, thought was necessary, vital, whatever the case may be, could he just issue an order to the military police, or would Momir Nikolic, chief of the security organ, would have to go to his immediate commander, Colonel Blagojevic, to get permission and have the authority to issue the order to the military police?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, as chief of security, according to this instruction, or rather, rules of service, I would have had the right to use the military police for the purposes and needs of the security organ. That's one thing I wish to point out. Should I choose to use the military police as a security organ, or rather, for the needs of the security organ, I know exactly what to do, which means I can't, for example, take a squad or patrol of military police officers for the needs of the security organ without obtaining authorisation from the commander that this would, indeed, be needed for performing tasks from my competence as chief of security. Let me clarify this: Very frequently, or rather, sometimes, occasionally it is necessary that military police officers as they go about their task, or rather, the chief of security would not be wearing uniform, badge, or anything at all. In that case, I would have to ask the officer whether I could have one, two, three, four, several policemen, as many as I need to carry out the task. That's one of your questions. And the second question was could I get the military police to do some work for me without consulting the commander previously? I think I've explained this on a number of occasions. The commander of the unit within whose composition the military police is guides and commands the military police, which means that the commander of the brigade, unit, sets tasks, assigns tasks to the military police unit. In that case, Momir Nikolic is responsible to the commander in the sense of making proposals regarding the best use to which these police units may be put, to make suggestions and for this unit to be kept in maximum combat readiness and prepared to carry out its potential task. But I have no authority to order to do anything that springs to my mind. The commander would define the task following my proposal or not. But of course, I, too, have a role to play in terms of professional guidance surrounding the implementation of a task.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I think with that, we can take our break. Well, it's up to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll resume at 3.00. --- Luncheon recess taken at 1.48 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I believe we were on the service regulations of the military police. It has been marked for identification purposes as D15/1. Okay, I just briefly want to touch on the section in chapter 3 starting with Article 17. So if you could be so kind as to go to Article 17, just look at it. And just so you know, I'll be asking you after that to look at 22, 23, 24, and 25. So if you could just give it a quick look, and we'll proceed when you're ready.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, excuse me, you said Article 17.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. First look at Article 17. Just look at that.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well. I've read through Article 17, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. It would be fair to say that this is just a general overview of the jurisdiction of the military police, Article 17.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, like it reads.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. Now, yesterday when we were discussing this order that was prepared by your commander, and in particular, when we were discussing paragraph 5.6.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And for the record, I'm referring to the -- what has been previously marked as D17/1 for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, it was your opinion as the former chief of intelligence and security of the Bratunac Brigade that this was an illegal use of the military police platoon?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, will you please just tell me what you're referring to in this order, what specifically. The brigade commander's order.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And if you could please also tell me...

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Would you please look at 5.6.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm looking at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. In that particular article, it designates the military police platoon to be the reserve, the reserve for the brigade, that is, while this order is in effect. In other words, the attack on Srebrenica. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, here it says: "Reserve military police platoon, have it in the area of the 1st Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade command post, ready to deploy if need be."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So they would be the reserve, and they would be located, unless told otherwise, or called upon, but they would be located at the brigade command post, and that would be in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, yesterday you registered some rather strong objections, if I may characterise the way at least I perceived your remarks, with respect to the usage of the military police platoon as a reserve. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I recall that you also indicated that in your opinion, it was an illegal or unlawful use of the military police platoon. Do you recall stating that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I believe that's a mischaracterisation of what he said. And there's obviously a clear record of what he said. So I think if there's going to be this kind of specific reference to yesterday, that it would be best in this context to use exactly what he said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, you are right. But let us hear what the witness is going to tell us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Mr. Karnavas, I can't quote precisely what I said yesterday, but I can try to paraphrase what I said and give you my general opinion on something like this being included in an order by the commander. The conclusion I can draw on the basis of this in relation to item 17, for example, I can't square this with any possible engagement by the military police as reserve in a brigade. I'm just not able to do it. That's one thing that I think is wrong here. Secondly, in my understanding, if brigade units are to engage in combat such as the battalions in this case, the 1st, the 2nd, the 3rd, and the 4th, in my understanding, these are units participating in active combat operations or attacks, or whatever mission it may be. It doesn't really matter. So if you put a military police platoon as reserve, then the only conclusion I can draw from that is that this is a reserve military police platoon being used for active combat activity, or operations.
